title: Undo without guessing
outcome: Choose restore, reset, revert, or reflog from what must be preserved.
cue: Preserve first. Inspect second. Move last.
version: Modern Git; check git --version for command availability

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: You reset a branch and realize a useful commit disappeared from the log. Recover access without destroying current work.

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: A bad commit is already on a shared branch. Why might revert be easier for teammates than reset plus force-push?

trace.title: Inspect state
trace.detail: Start with the question: what must stay? Working edits, staged changes, published history, and untracked files are different things. Inspect status and diffs, then preserve important work before experimenting.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
A soft reset moves the branch while keeping index/working content. A mixed reset also resets the index. A hard reset can discard tracked working changes. None should be run by habit.

Recovery starts by naming the old reachable commit with a rescue branch. Inspect it separately. A deleted untracked file that was never stored in Git is outside reflog’s promise. Seek editor/filesystem backups instead.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: git clean removes untracked content; reflog may not help. Do not use clean or reset --hard as generic “fix Git” commands. Reverting a merge also needs a deliberate mainline choice and affects future merge behavior.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Choose restore, reset, revert, or reflog from what must be preserved. Give a concrete failure example.
